questions.q: What problem do hybrid control-plane technologies like Azure Arc and AWS Outposts solve, beyond what connectivity and identity already handle?
options: They replace the need for any network connectivity between on-prem and cloud
They provide a new identity provider separate from Active Directory
They lower the cost of on-premises hardware
They give unified management — policy, monitoring, inventory, RBAC — across infrastructure that physically lives in different places
questions.explain: Once connectivity and identity exist, the remaining gap is a single pane of glass for managing servers and clusters scattered across on-prem and multiple clouds — exactly what these control-plane technologies address.

questions.q: What actually happens to a server when it's onboarded to Azure Arc-enabled servers?
options: The Connected Machine agent registers it in Azure as a HybridCompute resource, so Azure Policy, Defender for Cloud, and Monitor can govern it without moving it
The server's workload is automatically migrated into an Azure VM
The server is physically shipped to an Azure data center
The server's operating system is replaced with Azure-specific firmware
questions.explain: Arc projects the server as an Azure resource via the Connected Machine agent; the server stays exactly where it is, but Azure's governance tools can now reach it.

options: A monitoring dashboard for tracking on-premises servers from the AWS console
A virtual machine image that emulates AWS services on any hardware
A software agent that connects any on-prem server to AWS's control plane
Actual AWS compute and storage hardware (a rack or a compact server) installed on-premises or in a colo, run through the same APIs as AWS proper
questions.explain: Outposts is physical AWS hardware installed in the customer's own facility, managed as an extension of a home AWS Region using identical APIs, CLI, and console.

questions.q: What is the core structural difference between Azure Arc and AWS Outposts?
options: Arc extends Azure's management plane out to infrastructure you already own; Outposts brings actual AWS hardware physically into your facility
Arc only supports Linux servers, while Outposts only supports Windows servers
Outposts is a free service, while Arc requires a paid license for every server
Arc and Outposts are functionally identical products marketed under different names
questions.explain: Arc is a software control-plane layer reaching out to govern existing infrastructure; Outposts is genuine AWS hardware brought in-house. They solve similar problems from opposite directions.

questions.q: Which capability is specifically associated with Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes, according to this lesson?
options: Automatically converting any container into a serverless AWS Lambda function
Replacing the Kubernetes API server with a proprietary Azure API
Connecting any CNCF-conformant cluster to Azure for GitOps-based configuration via Flux and governance through Azure Policy for Kubernetes
Running only on AKS clusters that are already native to Azure
questions.explain: Arc-enabled Kubernetes connects any conformant cluster — on-prem, another cloud, or the edge — to Azure, enabling Flux-based GitOps and the same Azure Policy for Kubernetes engine used against native AKS.
